sourceFacts.fact: Cord clamping removes low-resistance placental circulation and raises systemic vascular resistance.

sources.title: Fetal Physiology and the Transition to Extrauterine Life (peer-reviewed review, PMC)

sourceFacts.fact: Lung expansion and increased oxygen lower pulmonary vascular resistance and increase pulmonary blood flow.

targetQuestion: What happens to systemic and pulmonary vascular resistance during neonatal transition?
targetAnswer: Cord clamping raises SVR while lung aeration lowers PVR.
